question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with the Separation of judiciary from executive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 50 is a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) under Part IV of the Indian Constitution. It directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State. (अनुच्छेद 50 — न्यायपालिका का कार्यपालिका से पृथक्करण)

 

• The objective is to ensure the independence of the judiciary so that judicial functions are free from executive interference or control.

 

• Being a DPSP, Article 50 is non-justiciable (Article 37) — it cannot be enforced directly by courts — but it is fundamental to the governance of the country and has guided reforms like separating the judicial magistracy from the executive magistracy under the CrPC, 1973.

 

• Article 50 reflects the doctrine of separation of powers, though India follows a partial (not strict) separation of powers among its organs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• DPSPs (Articles 36–51) are borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a welfare state.

 

• Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies for enforcement of Fundamental Rights, unlike DPSPs which are only guiding principles for governance.

 

NOTE

 

• 41 (Option 1): Directs the State to secure the right to work, education and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement.

 

• 51 (Option 2): Directs the State to promote international peace and security and maintain just and honourable relations between nations.

 

• 40 (Option 3): Directs the State to organise village panchayats and endow them with powers necessary for self-government.

question: World Bank approved USD 350 million aid in May 2022 for the “Systems Reform Endeavors for Transformed Health Achievement” (SRESTHA) for ______ state in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The World Bank approved a USD 350 million loan for the "Systems Reform Endeavors for Transformed Health Achievement in Gujarat" (SRESTHA-G) project to strengthen the state's primary healthcare and disease surveillance systems. (गुजरात स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली सुधार परियोजना)

 

• The project aims to make Gujarat's health system more resilient to future health emergencies/pandemics, and to improve access to and quality of primary healthcare services, especially for vulnerable populations.

 

• It also focuses on strengthening disease surveillance mechanisms, human resources for health, and governance of the state's health system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The World Bank has supported several state-specific health/social sector projects in India, such as projects in Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Andhra Pradesh, each tailored to that state's needs.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Not the state associated with the SRESTHA project; a distractor option.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Not the state associated with the SRESTHA project; a distractor option.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Not the state associated with the SRESTHA project; a distractor option.

question: The ______ of a ray is the angle measured from the reflected ray to the normal surface.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Angle of Reflection.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The angle of reflection is the angle measured between the reflected ray and the normal (the perpendicular line) to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence. (परावर्तन कोण)

 

• As per the Law of Reflection, the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection (∠i = ∠r), and both are measured from the normal, not from the surface itself.

 

• The incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Reflection can be regular (specular), from smooth polished surfaces like mirrors, producing a clear image, or irregular (diffused), from rough surfaces, scattering light in many directions.

 

NOTE

 

• Angle of Diffusion (Option 1): Not a standard term in the laws of reflection; diffusion relates to the scattering of light by rough surfaces or particles.

 

• Angle of Incidence (Option 3): The angle between the incident ray (the ray falling on the surface) and the normal, before reflection occurs.

 

• Angle of Refraction (Option 4): The angle between the refracted ray and the normal, formed when light bends while passing from one transparent medium into another.

question: ______ won the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Max Verstappen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing, Netherlands) won the 2022 Japanese Grand Prix, held at the Suzuka Circuit on 9 October 2022.

 

• The race was heavily affected by rain and was red-flagged; Verstappen's win at this race also confirmed him as the 2022 Formula 1 World Champion, his second consecutive title after 2021.

 

• Formula 1 is the highest class of international racing for open-wheel single-seater formula racing cars.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Verstappen went on to win the 2023 Japanese Grand Prix as well, and has won multiple F1 World Championships in the following seasons.

 

NOTE

 

• Charles Leclerc (Option 1): Ferrari driver; finished as runner-up at the 2022 Japanese Grand Prix.

 

• Sergio Perez (Option 2): Verstappen's Red Bull teammate during the 2022 season.

 

• Carlos Sainz Jr. (Option 4): Ferrari driver during the 2022 F1 season.

question: Which city existed in the Indus valley civilization?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harappa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harappa, located on the banks of the Ravi river in present-day Punjab, Pakistan, was one of the major cities of the Indus Valley Civilization (also called the Harappan Civilization, since it was the first site discovered, in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni).

 

• The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilization (c. 2500–1900 BCE) known for its urban planning, drainage systems, standardized weights and measures, and script (still undeciphered).

 

• Other major Indus Valley sites include Mohenjodaro, Lothal, Dholavira, Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi and Chanhudaro.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mohenjodaro ("Mound of the Dead"), on the Indus river in Sindh, Pakistan, is famous for the Great Bath and is the largest Indus Valley site.

 

• Lothal in Gujarat had a dockyard, indicating maritime trade, while Dholavira is known for its unique water conservation system and signboard.

 

NOTE

 

• Dwarka (Option 1): An ancient city in Gujarat associated with Lord Krishna in Hindu mythology, not an Indus Valley site.

 

• Sanchi (Option 3): Famous for its Buddhist stupas built under Ashoka, in Madhya Pradesh, not related to the Indus Valley Civilization.

 

• Muziris (Option 4): An ancient port city on the Malabar Coast (Kerala) known for Indo-Roman trade, not part of the Indus Valley Civilization.

question: The JALDOOT application launched in September 2022 is used by Gram Rojgar Sahyak to measure _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is water level in well.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The JALDOOT mobile application was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development in September 2022 to measure and record groundwater levels in wells in villages across India.

 

• Gram Rojgar Sahayaks (village employment assistants under MGNREGA) are required to measure the water level in two identified wells per Gram Panchayat, twice a year (pre-monsoon and post-monsoon), and upload this data on a central server through the app.

 

• The data collected helps track groundwater trends and supports planning of water conservation and MGNREGA-related water works.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• JALDOOT complements other groundwater-monitoring efforts, such as those of the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), by providing hyper-local, village-level data.

 

NOTE

 

• Rainfall (Option 1): Measured by rain gauges maintained by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), not by the JALDOOT app.

 

• Crop yield (Option 3): Assessed through agricultural surveys and remote sensing, not through JALDOOT.

 

• Humidity (Option 4): Measured by hygrometers, unrelated to the JALDOOT app's purpose.

question: In which year was the Arms Act passed in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1959.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arms Act, 1959 was enacted by the Parliament of India to consolidate and amend the law relating to arms and ammunition in India.

 

• It replaced the earlier colonial-era Indian Arms Act, 1878, and regulates the acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, and transport of firearms and ammunition.

 

• It is implemented alongside the Arms Rules framed under it, and works together with laws like the Explosives Act to regulate weapons in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arms Act, 1959 was significantly amended in 2019, increasing penalties and reducing the permissible number of licensed firearms per person from three to two.

 

NOTE

 

• 1951 (Option 1): Not the year of the Arms Act; several other laws, like the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, were passed in India in 1951.

 

• 1955 (Option 2): Not the year of the Arms Act.

 

• 1964 (Option 4): Not the year of the Arms Act.

question: ______ is the key circuit board holding the essential processing parts of a computer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Motherboard.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The motherboard is the primary/main circuit board of a computer that holds and interconnects the essential processing components, such as the CPU, RAM, chipset, and expansion slots.

 

• It provides communication pathways (buses) that allow data to travel between the various components of the computer.

 

• Other components like the CPU, RAM, and storage devices are all connected to and mounted on the motherboard.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The motherboard also houses the BIOS/UEFI firmware, which initializes hardware during the booting process before handing control to the operating system.

 

NOTE

 

• Firmware (Option 1): Low-level software embedded in hardware devices (like BIOS) to control basic functions; it is not a circuit board.

 

• Central Processing Unit (Option 2): The "brain" of the computer that executes instructions; it is mounted on the motherboard, not the board itself.

 

• Random Access Memory (Option 3): A temporary, volatile memory component that also sits on the motherboard but is not the main circuit board itself.

question: Which is the highest plateau in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tibet plateau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tibetan Plateau, also known as the "Roof of the World", is the highest and largest plateau in the world, with an average elevation exceeding 4,500 metres above sea level. (तिब्बत का पठार — विश्व का सबसे ऊँचा पठार)

 

• It covers a vast area across Tibet (China) and parts of neighbouring regions, and is the source of many major Asian rivers, including the Indus, Brahmaputra, Yangtze, and Yellow rivers.

 

• It is bounded by the Himalayas to the south and the Kunlun mountains to the north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Deccan Plateau in India is a large volcanic plateau formed mainly by basaltic lava flows (Deccan Traps) during the late Cretaceous to early Paleocene period.

 

NOTE

 

• East African Plateau (Option 1): A large plateau in East Africa, home to the Great Rift Valley, but much lower in elevation than the Tibetan Plateau.

 

• Deccan plateau (Option 2): A triangular plateau in peninsular India, bounded by the Western and Eastern Ghats, but not the highest in the world.

 

• Western plateau (Option 3): Not a globally recognized term for the world's highest plateau; a distractor option.

question: Which of the following is not a regional name for East Coast (or part of it) of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malabar Coast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's East Coast (along the Bay of Bengal) is regionally known by names such as the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu–Andhra Pradesh stretch) and the Utkal Coast (Odisha), and is also loosely referred to along the Tamil Nadu coast.

 

• The Malabar Coast, in contrast, lies along the West Coast of India (bordering the Arabian Sea), covering parts of Kerala and Karnataka.

 

• Thus, Malabar Coast is the odd one out, as it does not refer to any part of the East Coast.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's West Coast is also known by regional names such as the Konkan Coast (Maharashtra–Goa) and the Kannad/Canara Coast (Karnataka), apart from the Malabar Coast (Kerala).

 

NOTE

 

• Coromandel Coast (Option 1): The stretch of the East Coast from Chennai to Kanyakumari (parts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh).

 

• Tamil Nadu coast (Option 2): Part of the East Coast, falling within the broader Coromandel Coast region.

 

• Utkal coast (Option 3): The stretch of the East Coast along Odisha, historically known as Utkal.

question: _________ is an ancient martial art that originated in peninsular India as a part of military training for warriors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalaripayattu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalaripayattu is considered one of the oldest surviving martial arts in the world, originating in present-day Kerala (peninsular/South India) as part of the military training of warriors. (कलरीपायट्टु — केरल की प्राचीन युद्धकला)

 

• The name derives from "kalari" (meaning training ground/battlefield) and "payattu" (meaning fight/exercise/practice).

 

• It combines strikes, kicks, grappling, weaponry (like swords and spears), and healing techniques (marma therapy), and is traditionally taught in a "kalari" — a specially constructed training space.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalaripayattu is believed to have influenced other Asian martial arts through trade and cultural contacts over centuries.

 

NOTE

 

• Gatka (Option 1): A Sikh martial art from Punjab, traditionally performed with sticks or swords, often associated with Sikh warrior traditions.

 

• Muay Thai (Option 2): A striking martial art and combat sport originating in Thailand, known as the "art of eight limbs."

 

• Karate (Option 4): A striking martial art that originated in the Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa), Japan.

question: In October 2022, which among the following substances was mapped in abundance for the first time, by Chandrayaan-2, on moon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In October 2022, ISRO announced that the CLASS (Chandrayaan-2 Large Area Soft X-ray Spectrometer) instrument onboard Chandrayaan-2 mapped the abundance of sodium on the Moon's surface for the first time, using X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy.

 

• This mapping helps in understanding the exospheric processes of the Moon, as sodium is a volatile element that can escape into the Moon's thin exosphere.

 

• Chandrayaan-2, launched in 2019, consists of an Orbiter, Lander (Vikram) and Rover (Pragyan); although the lander crashed, the Orbiter continues to function and conduct valuable scientific studies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandrayaan-3, launched in 2023, successfully soft-landed near the Moon's south pole, building on data and experience from Chandrayaan-2.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrogen (Option 1): Water-ice/hydroxyl signatures were earlier detected by Chandrayaan-1's instruments, not this specific "first-time sodium mapping" finding.

 

• Chlorine (Option 2): Not the element referenced in this October 2022 finding.

 

• Oxygen (Option 3): Not the element referenced in this October 2022 finding.

question: Davis Cup is related with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Davis Cup is the premier international team competition in men's tennis, organized by the International Tennis Federation (ITF).

 

• It is contested annually between national teams in a knockout format, and is often referred to as the "World Cup of Tennis."

 

• It was first held in 1900, originally as a challenge between the United States and Great Britain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The women's equivalent of the Davis Cup is the Billie Jean King Cup (formerly the Fed Cup).

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 1): Its major team events are the Thomas Cup (men) and Uber Cup (women), not the Davis Cup.

 

• Cricket (Option 2): Not associated with the Davis Cup, which is exclusively a tennis competition.

 

• Basketball (Option 3): Not associated with the Davis Cup.

question: Who wrote the famous novel "Durgeshnandini"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee (Chattopadhyay) wrote "Durgeshnandini" (1865), which is considered the first modern novel in Bengali literature. (दुर्गेशनन्दिनी — बंकिम चंद्र चट्टोपाध्याय की रचना)

 

• He was a celebrated Bengali novelist, poet and journalist, best known for his novel "Anandamath" (1882), which contains the song "Vande Mataram," later adopted as India's National Song.

 

• His works played a significant role in the growth of Bengali nationalism during the Indian freedom movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bankim Chandra also served as a Deputy Collector in British India and founded the literary magazine "Bangadarshan."

 

NOTE

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 1): Nobel laureate (1913, Literature) for "Gitanjali"; wrote India's National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana."

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (Option 2): Renowned educationist and social reformer, known for his work on widow remarriage and Bengali prose/education reforms.

 

• Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay (Option 4): Noted Bengali novelist, author of works like "Devdas" and "Parineeta."

question: Which among the following is correct about Reverse Repo Rate?
option_1: Reverse Repo Rate is a state in which the Value of Money is Falling and the Prices are rising, over a period of time.
option_2: When bank deposit it’s excess money in RBI then RBI provides some interest to that bank. This interest is known as Reverse Repo Rate.
option_3: When RBI provides a loan to the bank for short-term between 1 to 90 days, RBI takes some interest from the bank which is termed as Reverse Repo Rate.
option_4: When the money is borrowed or lent for more than a day up to 14 days it is called Reverse Repo Rate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is When bank deposit it's excess money in RBI then RBI provides some interest to that bank. This interest is known as Reverse Repo Rate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reverse Repo Rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) borrows money from commercial banks, by accepting their surplus/excess funds against government securities, and pays them interest in return. (रिवर्स रेपो रेट — RBI द्वारा बैंकों से उधार लेने की दर)

 

• It is a key tool of monetary policy used to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system, thereby helping to control inflation.

 

• When RBI increases the Reverse Repo Rate, banks are incentivized to park more funds with RBI (as they earn higher interest), which reduces the money supply in the economy.

 

• This is the opposite of the Repo Rate, which is the rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks against securities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Both the Repo Rate and Reverse Repo Rate are decided by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), which meets periodically (bi-monthly) to review key policy rates.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: This describes the concept of inflation (falling value of money and rising prices), not the Reverse Repo Rate.

 

• Option 3: This describes the Repo Rate, where RBI lends short-term funds to banks against securities and charges interest.

 

• Option 4: This describes a general short-term borrowing/lending arrangement, not the specific definition of Reverse Repo Rate; it does not correctly define the term.

question: The plains from Ambala to the Sunderban stretch over nearly 1800 km, but the fall in its slope is hardly ______ metres.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 300.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Northern Plains of India, stretching over nearly 1,800 km from Ambala/Saharanpur to the Sunderban delta, are formed by the depositional work of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers and their tributaries.

 

• Despite this enormous horizontal extent, the plains have an exceptionally gentle slope, with the overall fall in elevation across this stretch being hardly about 300 metres, making it one of the flattest and most extensive alluvial plains in the world.

 

• This flatness, combined with fertile alluvial soil, makes the Northern Plains one of the most densely populated and agriculturally productive regions of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Northern Plains are commonly divided into the Punjab Plains, Rajasthan Plains, Ganga Plains, and Brahmaputra Plains based on regional and drainage characteristics.

 

NOTE

 

• 550 (Option 1): Not the figure associated with this fact about the Northern Plains' slope.

 

• 600 (Option 3): Not the figure associated with this fact about the Northern Plains' slope.

 

• 450 (Option 4): Not the figure associated with this fact about the Northern Plains' slope.

question: In which of the following modes of data transmission, can the data flow in both directions but in only one direction at a time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Half-duplex.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In half-duplex data transmission, data can flow in both directions, but only one direction at a time — that is, when one device is transmitting, the other can only receive, and vice versa.

 

• A common example is a walkie-talkie, where only one person can speak at a time while the other listens.

 

• This mode makes efficient use of the communication channel compared to simplex, while still avoiding the complexity/cost of simultaneous two-way transmission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Full-duplex communication (like a telephone call) allows simultaneous two-way data flow, offering the most efficient use of bandwidth for real-time communication.

 

NOTE

 

• Simplex (Option 2): Data flows in only one direction, never the reverse — e.g., radio or television broadcasting, keyboard-to-CPU transmission.

 

• Full-duplex (Option 3): Data flows in both directions simultaneously — e.g., telephone communication.

 

• Quarter-duplex (Option 4): Not a standard/recognized data transmission mode; a distractor option.

question: Which among the following is the highest peak in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanchenjunga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kanchenjunga, at 8,586 metres, located on the India–Nepal border in the state of Sikkim, is the highest peak located within Indian territory and the third-highest mountain peak in the world.

 

• It is part of the Great Himalayan range and is considered sacred by the local Sikkimese and Nepali people.

 

• Mount Everest (world's highest) and K2 (world's second-highest) lie outside India — Everest in Nepal/China, and K2 in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK) — hence they are not counted as peaks "in India."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kanchenjunga was first successfully climbed in 1955 by Joe Brown and George Band of a British expedition team.

 

NOTE

 

• Nanga Parbat (Option 2): The ninth-highest mountain in the world, located in Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan, not in India.

 

• Nanda Devi (Option 3): The second-highest peak located entirely within India (in Uttarakhand), after Kanchenjunga.

 

• Namcha Barwa (Option 4): A peak located in Tibet (China), at the eastern end of the Himalayas near the Brahmaputra's great bend.

question: In October 2022, according to UN Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), which country has the largest number of poor people worldwide?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2022, released jointly by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) in October 2022, India had the largest number of multidimensionally poor people in the world, estimated at around 228.9 million (22.89 crore) people.

 

• The report also highlighted a positive trend: the number of poor people in India fell by about 415 million between 2005-06 and 2019-21, indicating significant poverty reduction over that period.

 

• The MPI measures poverty across health, education, and standard of living indicators, going beyond just income-based measures of poverty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nigeria had the second-largest number of MPI-poor people in this 2022 report, followed by countries like Ethiopia, Pakistan, and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

 

NOTE

 

• Nigeria (Option 1): Recorded the second-highest number of MPI-poor people in this report, not the largest.

 

• Indonesia (Option 2): Not among the countries with the highest number of MPI-poor people in this 2022 report.

 

• Pakistan (Option 3): Had a notable number of MPI-poor people, but fewer than both India and Nigeria.

question: Neelima performs Kalbeliya dance form. Which state does this dance form belong to?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalbeliya is a traditional folk dance form performed by the Kalbeliya community (a snake-charmer tribe) of Rajasthan. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• Dancers, dressed in black flowing skirts (ghagra) embroidered with silver ribbons, perform swift and graceful movements that mimic the movements of a snake.

 

• In 2010, Kalbeliya folk songs and dances of Rajasthan were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Chari, and Bhavai.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Bhangra (male) and Giddha (female), not Kalbeliya.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Chholiya and Langvir Nritya, not Kalbeliya.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): Known for classical/folk dances like Odissi and Gotipua, not Kalbeliya.

question: Which of the following music instruments are solid instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghana Vadya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian classical musicology classifies instruments into four broad categories: Tata Vadya (stringed), Sushira Vadya (wind), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with a membrane), and Ghana Vadya (solid/self-sounding).

 

• Ghana Vadya instruments are solid instruments that do not require tuning and produce sound through their own solid vibrating material (idiophones) — examples include manjira (cymbals), jaltarang, and ghatam.

 

• They are among the oldest categories of musical instruments used in Indian tradition, often for rhythmic accompaniment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This four-fold classification of Indian musical instruments is based on the ancient treatise Natya Shastra, attributed to sage Bharata.

 

NOTE

 

• Tata Vadya (Option 1): Stringed instruments, e.g., sitar, veena, sarod, violin.

 

• Avanaddha Vadya (Option 3): Percussion instruments with a membrane stretched over them, e.g., tabla, mridangam, dholak.

 

• Sushira Vadya (Option 4): Wind instruments, e.g., flute (bansuri), shehnai, harmonium.

question: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) is the ambitious program launched by Government of India in 2018 to provide ______ access to the most vulnerable sections.
solution_text:
The correct answer is healthcare.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), launched by the Government of India in 2018 (under the umbrella scheme Ayushman Bharat), aims to provide free and cashless healthcare access to the most economically vulnerable sections of society.

 

• It provides a health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization, benefiting around 10.74 crore poor and vulnerable families (roughly the bottom 40% of the population).

 

• PM-JAY is often described as the world's largest government-funded health insurance/assurance scheme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other pillar of Ayushman Bharat is the establishment of Health and Wellness Centres to provide comprehensive primary healthcare closer to people's homes.

 

NOTE

 

• Services (Option 2): Too generic/vague; PM-JAY's specific stated aim is to provide healthcare access, not "services" broadly.

 

• Agricultural (Option 3): Not related to PM-JAY, which is a health insurance scheme.

 

• Industrial (Option 4): Not related to PM-JAY, which is a health insurance scheme.

question: A ball possesses 3000 units of momentum. What would be the ball’s new momentum if its velocity was doubled?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6000 units.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Momentum (p) of an object is calculated using the formula: p = m × v, where m is the mass and v is the velocity of the object.

 

• If the velocity of the ball is doubled while its mass remains constant, its momentum will also double, since momentum is directly proportional to velocity.

 

• Given the initial momentum is 3000 units, doubling the velocity gives: new momentum = 2 × 3000 = 6000 units.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Momentum is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction, and its SI unit is kg·m/s.

 

NOTE

 

• 3000 units (Option 1): This is the original momentum, unchanged — incorrect, since velocity was doubled.

 

• 20000 units (Option 3): Not obtained through the correct proportional relationship between momentum and velocity.

 

• 9000 units (Option 4): Not obtained through the correct proportional relationship between momentum and velocity (this would suggest a tripling, not doubling).

question: Who among the following appointed Aziz Khummar a wine distiller to high administrative post?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Tughluq.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muhammad bin Tughluq, the Sultan of Delhi (1325–1351 CE), was known for his controversial and experimental administrative policies, including appointing people from diverse and unconventional backgrounds — such as Aziz Khummar, a wine distiller — to high administrative posts. (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक — असामान्य प्रशासनिक नियुक्तियाँ)

 

• This practice reflected his attempt to select officials based on merit/ability rather than birth or traditional aristocratic lineage, though it was heavily criticized by contemporary chroniclers like Ziauddin Barani.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughluq is also remembered for other bold (and often failed) experiments, such as the transfer of capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token currency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveller, visited India during Muhammad bin Tughluq's reign and served as a Qazi (judge) in Delhi under him.

 

NOTE

 

• Alauddin Khalji (Option 1): Delhi Sultan known for market control reforms (Diwan-i-Riyasat) and repelling Mongol invasions, not for this appointment.

 

• Jalaluddin Khalji (Option 3): Founder of the Khalji dynasty, known for his relatively lenient/tolerant rule.

 

• Firuz Shah Tughluq (Option 4): Successor of Muhammad bin Tughluq, known for public welfare works, irrigation canals, and reviving the iqta system.

question: Which among the following is a bacterial disease?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leprosy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Leprosy (Hansen's disease) is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium leprae, which primarily affects the skin, peripheral nerves, and mucous membranes. (कुष्ठ रोग — जीवाणु जनित रोग)

 

• It is a chronic infectious disease that, left untreated, can cause progressive and permanent damage to the skin, nerves, limbs and eyes.

 

• It is curable with Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT), which is provided free of cost under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India observes Anti-Leprosy Day on 30th January, coinciding with the death anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, who worked extensively for the welfare of leprosy patients.

 

NOTE

 

• Rabies (Option 1): A viral disease caused by the rabies virus, transmitted mainly through the bite of infected animals (e.g., dogs).

 

• Malaria (Option 3): Caused by the Plasmodium parasite, transmitted through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

 

• Ebola (Option 4): A severe viral hemorrhagic fever caused by the Ebola virus.
